content.comment_body: This is an older discussion, but I have a similar project setup. I’m working with two small 100W 230VAC fans and want to adjust their speed using [product_name] with AI and AQ modules. How can this be done? Would a motor controller be necessary? Any suggestions?

I came across a German website: MVS-1. I can't provide pricing—contact the company directly for that. Refer to the attached German datasheet for details. Description: The device is designed for automatic, stepless speed control of voltage-adjustable motors (230V, 50Hz) on fans and pumps, utilizing a 0-10V or 0-20mA control signal. Installation involves wiring as shown in the provided circuit diagram. An external transmitter (not included, see group 2/5) supplies the 0-10V or 0-20mA signal needed for control, with configuration selections available on jumper 16. Minimum speed (60-160V) can be set via potentiometer 21; maximum speed (150-230VAC) via potentiometer 22. Potentiometer 20 lets you choose if the fan switches off at a signal between 0-4V or 10-6V, according to switch 16’s position. Switch 18 enables either a 'hard start' (maximum speed for 8-10 seconds) or a normal start. The unit mounts on a DIN rail.

A suggestion was made to use an external motor controller that responds to 0-10V or 0-20mA signals, noting that the [product_name] can provide the necessary control signals, though additional compatible hardware will be required.
